findings.original: `sys.intern()` makes equal strings share one object.
findings.correction: `sys.intern()` returns a canonical interned string; keep and use that return value. It does not rewrite existing references to equal non-interned strings.
findings.reason: Interning does not mutate all equivalent strings.

findings.original: Each character on screen stores a reference to the shared glyph plus its own position.
findings.correction: Each character on screen can store a reference to a shared glyph plus its own position. This sequential example reuses one cached object, but simultaneous first calls to `lru_cache` can construct duplicates. The unbounded cache also retains objects until cleared.
findings.reason: Thread-safe cache does not guarantee once-only factory execution.

findings.original: modifying a collection while iterating over it is unsafe (dicts raise `RuntimeError`; lists silently skip items).
findings.correction: structural mutation during iteration can invalidate traversal. Adding or deleting dictionary keys may raise `RuntimeError`; replacing values for existing keys need not. List insertions/deletions may skip or repeat elements, while replacing an existing element does not inherently invalidate iteration.
findings.reason: Not all mutations raise or skip.

findings.original: send an idempotency key so a retried request is recognised and applied once.
findings.correction: use the same idempotency key on retries, with server-side atomic deduplication tied to the effect and a retention policy covering the retry window. Sending a key alone does not enforce this.

findings.original: Encryption removes visible repetition; ciphertext is indistinguishable from random.
findings.correction: Properly used modern encryption hides useful plaintext redundancy, so compressing its ciphertext generally saves little. Encryption alone is not a universal promise that every format or mode produces random-looking bytes.
findings.reason: ECB and format metadata defeat universal ciphertext statement.

findings.correction: Normal successful model save() calls emit post_save for creation and updates. Bulk update APIs and skipped saves do not necessarily emit it; the question concerns receiver lifetime.
